# Goban Studio v7.0.0

v7 is about a coach that keeps up with you: a weekly training plan built
from your own games, reports that make themselves, problem collections you
bring in from SGF files, an engine that always answers your move first, a
human-style ladder without a gap, and a larger opening book.

## Download and first launch

<!-- first-launch -->
| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| macOS (Intel) | `GobanStudio-macOS-x64.dmg` or `.zip` | See the package README. |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | See the package README. |
<!-- /first-launch -->

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of every file. Windows on ARM runs the x64
build under the system's emulation. v6 can update itself to v7 from
Settings → About.

## An important fix: SGF coordinates

Up to v6 the app read and wrote SGF coordinates without the letter *i*, but
the SGF standard (FF[4]) uses a..s *with* the i. Records from other programs
were therefore read wrongly: stones in the 9th and 10th columns were put on
the same line and the last column was never used. The 20 built-in classic
games were affected too — all of them now load without a single illegal-move
warning.

- v7 reads and writes standard coordinates.
- Records saved by Goban Studio before v7 (the library, mistake drills,
  backups) are recognised by their `AP[Goban Studio:…]` stamp and read the
  old way, so nothing you saved changes.
- **What cannot be repaired:** a game you imported from another program
  before v7 was misread when it was imported and saved as misread; the
  original file was not kept. Import the original file again to get the
  correct game.

## A training plan

- Today shows **This week's focus**: one or two themes (ladders, cuts, eye
  space, races, endgame, …) chosen from your analysed games and your problem
  results, with the reason in plain words ("Lost ≈18 points here in your
  last 6 games").
- The Daily five is filled with problems and drills for that focus at your
  solving level. The focus stays the same for the week; this week's games
  shape next week's.
- With fewer than three analysed games it says so instead of guessing.

## Reports that make themselves

- After a game the report is prepared in the background — you no longer
  wait on the result screen. It shows how your strength estimate moved, and
  the exported image includes it.
- **Analyse all** in the Library prepares the reports of older games one by
  one; you can stop it at any time.
- A report of a game between two people lets you choose whose mistakes to
  practise (Black or White), instead of drilling both sides.

## Problem collections

- Practice → **Your collections**: import SGF problems — one per file, many
  per file, or many files at once.
- The app works out each problem's goal (kill, live, capture, connect) and
  proves the answer with its solver. Only problems whose proved answer
  agrees with the file are added; a file answer proved wrong is shown with
  the refutation; problems that could not be proved are listed in the import
  report with the reason, never added as if proved.
- Collections keep progress and review timing like the built-in problems
  and are part of backups.

## The engine answers your move first

- Analysis is now scheduled: the computer's move comes first, then what you
  are looking at, then live analysis, then background work (reports,
  Analyse all).
- Work that is no longer needed is cancelled — leaving a game or a review
  stops its analysis instead of letting it hold up the next game.
- Settings → Opponents and analysis lists what is working in the background, with a Stop button for each job.

## Strength

- **The human-style ladder has no gap**: it now reads 30, 29, 23, 18, 12,
  7 kyu, 1 kyu and 6 dan (before: a jump from ≈12 kyu to ≈3 kyu). The
  settings were measured on GitHub's build machines — 708 games on 19×19
  and 824 on 9×9, pooled with v6's 426. From 25 kyu to 7 kyu the human-style
  and the standard levels now show the same labels.
- Human-style 5 kyu now plays as ≈7 kyu, 15 kyu as ≈18 kyu, 1 kyu as ≈1
  kyu; the two top levels read ≈6 dan and ≈7 dan. `docs/strength.md` has
  every result with its 95 % interval and how to run it again.

## Opening book

- The opening book was evaluated again on GitHub's build machines.

## Fixes

- A problem answered wrong and then right is now recorded as solved (not
  as a clean solve; the miss still sets the review timing).
- With a screen reader, the row, column and board keys read the whole
  widened problem window, not only the problem's own area.
- Report: the key moments keep their words for screen readers; each phase
  table is named for Black or White.

## Checked together

Every page added since v5 is now checked in all four languages, in light
and dark, with and without larger text: the accessibility audit, no
untranslated text, no clipped buttons, nothing scrolling sideways, and at
most one main button per screen.

## Known limits

- The builds are not code-signed (no certificates yet). The update
  checksum guards against damaged or wrong downloads; it is not a
  signature.
- Not yet checked by people: a usability test, a strong player's review of
  the advanced course and the explorer, a native-speaker review of the
  Chinese, Korean and Japanese text, and a real screen-reader session.
- Imported problems do not enter the Daily five yet. The desktop app can
  pick many files at once but not a whole folder. Wide-open problems (for
  example ladders) usually cannot be proved and are not imported.
- The training plan has no theme for tempo mistakes; drills from reviewed
  classic games count toward your weak themes.
- A background search that has already started runs to its end before the
  computer's move (the wait is short; it is not interrupted).
- The standard ladder and its 10-kyu anchor were not measured again. The
  1 kyu human-style level rests on one run of 64 games, and above 4 dan the
  labels are the furthest from the anchor. On 9×9 the human-style 2 dan
  level plays about even with the standard 2 dan; the labels follow 19×19.
- The counting solver ignores ko threats; endgame problems avoid ko.

## Your data

Everything from v6 carries over. See "SGF coordinates" above for games
imported from other programs before v7.
